body:
My thought here was to use the TS/JS/JSON formatters to hit anything in the docs directory that was directly written by us, but it seems that there are no such files (or they all exist in .vuepress).

Do we want to get rid of the typescript and JSON formatters in that case? (The TOML one should stay because it's used to format TOML in Markdown code blocks, which we have a ton of).

We should probably add `"**/*.toml"` if we'd like to have Cargo.toml, clippy.toml, and Cross.toml to be formatted.
```suggestion
  "includes": ["docs/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,cjs,mjs,json,md,toml}", "**/*.{md,toml}"],
```

```suggestion
```
I'd suggest removing "docs/.vuepress" from exclusions as they're all hand-written files. `docs/.vuepress/config.js` in particular, which we edit every time we update site translations.
If it doesn't slow things down meaningfully, having it format `docs/.vuepress/config.js` is nice.
I assume we'll have to manually update these plugins every so often?

+Starship source files are formatted with [rustfmt](https://crates.io/crates/rustfmt-nightly), using the default configuration. Markdown files are formatted with [dprint](https://dprint.dev), using the configurations contained in `.dprint.json`.
+
+Both formatters will run as part of the CI process. Unformatted code will fail a
+build, so it is suggested that you run rustfmt locally:
 
 ```sh
+# To format Rust source
 rustup component add rustfmt
 cargo fmt
+
+# To format documentation
+cargo install dprint
+dprint fmt
 ```
body: Dprint seems to have a rustfmt plugin. Is it worth unifying our formatting to all be handled by dprint?
I don't think speed is an issue at all (maybe if you have the starship directory on a network drive). I just wasn't sure if .vuepress was something we should format. Will add the directory.
Okay, I wasn't sure if those were handwritten of not.

I assume so. The perks of pre-1.0 software, I guess.

The `dprint` README says that the CLI tool will let us know when this needs to happen, and the release notes will provide an upgrade path, so we at least shouldn't be in a situation where upgrades break everything and we have no clue what's going on.

I had originally envisioned this as a docs-only change (which is why there's no Rust plugin and why only files within the docs folder are touched).

I think it should be very much possible to modify this to become a general-purpose format-as-much-as-we-can tool, but I should probably restructure the PR a little bit (particularly, which parts of CI are handled by the "code" workflow and which are handled by the "formatting" workflow) to achieve that.
